opening_message:
Ticket 1: Keith Mclaughlin (employee ID E032) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E032.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Keith Mclaughlin (E032), Analyst, full-time employee, requests write access to Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write access (admin requires owning role; Analyst does not own Source Code). Requested level is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E032 is a contractor with basic security training (HR note listed full-time; Security DB is authoritative here). Contractors with basic training max out at read; write requires advanced training. Recommend read.
reason: Security agent's note (authoritative for employment type) shows E032 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors max out at read without advanced training, and never admin. Since the requested write exceeds the maximum, grant the maximum allowed: read.

content.text:
Let me work through this ticket.

The employee is Keith Mclaughlin (E032), requesting write access to Source Code.

HR note: role Analyst, employment type full_time, recommend write for Source Code.

Security note: role Analyst (not looked up, same as HR), employment type contractor (looked up in Security DB, authoritative), security training basic, recommend read.

There's a conflict: HR says full-time, Security says contractor. The Security agent says their DB is authoritative for employment type.

Access policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns the system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin.

Analyst does not own Source Code (Engineer owns Source Code).

If full-time: max is write, requested write → grant write.
If contractor with basic training: max is read, requested write → grant read (maximum).

Security says contractor with basic training. Security DB authoritative. So the max is read. Requested write is above max, so grant read.

So the decision is read.

Submit decision with level "read" and reason citing security note: contractor, basic training, max read; requested write above max, grant read.
